title: The rise of ‘gray divorce,’ and why so many Boomers are splitting up late in life
titleZh: 为什么越来越多婴儿潮一代晚年离婚？
summary:
在美国，50岁及以上人群的离婚现象比以往任何时候都更为普遍，近年来，在所有的婚姻破裂案例中，近半数都来自步入中老年的X世代与婴儿潮一代。目前，全美约40%的离婚发生在50岁及以上的夫妻之间——这类离异被称为“银发离婚”。自疫情以来，这一惊人的比例始终居高不下，而在此之前，该趋势已经持续攀升了约40年。据《纽约时报》报道，1990年至2010年间，银发离婚的数量翻了一番，约占全美离婚总数的四分之一，此后继续走高，直至如今的四成。与此同时，尽管美国大多数年龄群体的离婚率呈下降趋势，但50岁及以上人群却未见回落。

来源：纽约邮报；作者：Alex Oliveira；原文发布时间：2026-06-25 19:59:00

paragraphs.contentEn: Americans age 50 and older are getting divorced more than ever, with almost half of all broken marriages in recent years coming from aging Gen Xers and Baby Boomers. Nearly 40% of all divorces nationwide are among couples 50 years and older — separations known as “gray divorces.” The alarming rate has held steady since the pandemic, but followed about four decades of increases. Gray divorces doubled between 1990 and 2010, until they comprised about one in four of all divorces nationally, and then climbed to today’s four in 10 rate, according to the New York Times. And though divorce has been dropping in most age groups across America, it has not among people 50 years and older.
paragraphs.contentZh: 在美国，50岁及以上人群的离婚现象比以往任何时候都更为普遍，近年来，在所有的婚姻破裂案例中，近半数都来自步入中老年的X世代与婴儿潮一代。目前，全美约40%的离婚发生在50岁及以上的夫妻之间——这类离异被称为“银发离婚”。自疫情以来，这一惊人的比例始终居高不下，而在此之前，该趋势已经持续攀升了约40年。据《纽约时报》报道，1990年至2010年间，银发离婚的数量翻了一番，约占全美离婚总数的四分之一，此后继续走高，直至如今的四成。与此同时，尽管美国大多数年龄群体的离婚率呈下降趋势，但50岁及以上人群却未见回落。

paragraphs.contentEn: Experts have given a variety of explanations for this phenomenon — including longer lifespans, people marrying older, “empty nester” syndrome, and even wives being less tolerant of insensitive spouses after menopause. But Michael Stutman, a top New York City divorce lawyer, thinks a “popular culture” shift around modern marriage expectations, coupled with staring down the barrel of mortality, could be playing a part. “The thing about people who are over 50 is that they’re getting cognizant that the fuel gauge is starting to go down to empty,” Stutman told The Post. “And there’s one thing money can’t buy, which is time.”
paragraphs.contentZh: 针对这一现象，专家们提出了多种解释——包括预期寿命延长、结婚年龄推迟、“空巢综合征”，甚至有说法认为，女性在更年期后对不够体贴的伴侣容忍度下降。不过，纽约顶尖离婚律师迈克尔·斯图特曼认为，“流行文化”对现代婚姻期待的重塑，加上直面生命终有尽头这一现实，或许也在其中发挥作用。斯图特曼在接受《纽约邮报》采访时表示：“年过半百的人开始意识到，自己人生的油量表正一点点见底。毕竟有一样东西是金钱买不到的，那就是时间。”

paragraphs.contentEn: “People finally realize that if they’re starting to drain the second half of the tank, if they have bucket list items or a wish list or whatever, they don’t want to spend the limited time that they may have left investing in something that they feel will not give them an appropriate rate of return,” he added. Stutman said the 40% rate felt higher than what he’s personally seen, but acknowledged that “the trend line for our practice, of seeing the age of our clients increasing, is definitely a thing.” One woman, 58-year-old Ruchi, said she decided to leave her husband after he completely forgot her 50th birthday. “You’ve put all these things aside because you’re a mom and you’re taking care of a family,” she said, “Then you think: Is that all I am good for? When did I stop being a person?”
paragraphs.contentZh: 斯图特曼接着说道：“人们最终意识到，当自己开始消耗人生下半箱油时，如果心里还有未竟的心愿或梦想，他们就不愿再把所剩无几的时间，投入到那些无法带来应有回报的人或事上了。”斯图特曼表示，40%这一比例高于他个人的直观感受，但他也承认：“从我们律所的业务情况来看，咨询客户的年龄越来越大，这确实是一个明显的趋势。”58岁的受访女性鲁奇表示，在丈夫完全忘记了她的50岁生日后，她最终决定结束这段婚姻。她说道：“当了母亲之后，你一直在照顾家庭，把自己的许多诉求都放到了一边。但到了后来你会开始反思：难道我的价值就只有这些吗？我是从什么时候起，不再是一个独立的个体了？”

paragraphs.contentEn: Ruchi also said she’s become much less tolerant of her forgetful husband after menopause — which is a well-documented phenomenon. “I actually thought I was crazy, because I was irritated at everything,” she told the Times. Another possible motivator could be a societal shift toward getting married later. People are increasingly getting hitched in their 30s or 40s, instead of the old norm of marriage in people’s 20s — which Stutman said would naturally affect the age people are if their marriages fall apart. “Over the last 20 years, the age of people getting into their first marriage has expanded. It has been elongating,” Stutman said.
paragraphs.contentZh: 鲁奇还提到，更年期之后，她对健忘丈夫的容忍度大不如前——这一现象也早有大量研究佐证。她在接受《纽约时报》采访时说：“我一度以为自己是不是疯了，因为几乎所有事情都会让我感到烦躁。”晚婚的社会趋势或许是另一个潜在诱因。如今，人们越来越多地选择在三四十岁结婚，而非像过去那样普遍在二十多岁成家——斯图特曼指出，这自然也会影响到人们婚姻破裂时的年龄。斯图特曼表示：“过去20年来，人们初婚的年龄跨度在不断扩大，且整体呈现不断推迟的趋势。”

paragraphs.contentEn: “So if you believe there’s some inherent process that goes on in a marriage that leads people to end it after their children are in college, or if there’s a 15- or 20-year-old lifetime — their first marriages are 20 years old by the time they’re 50, as opposed to when it would have been maybe 40,” he said. But the gray divorce rates don’t mean romance is over for the silver-haired. About 14% of Americans in their 60s have hit up the dating apps, according to a 2023 Pew Research Center survey. And 12% of Americans 70 years and older have also used dating apps, the Times reported.
paragraphs.contentZh: 斯图特曼补充说：“所以，如果你认为婚姻中存在某种固有的演变规律，会让夫妻在孩子上大学后就选择结束婚姻，又或者认为一段婚姻的自然寿命就是15到20年左右——那么，当第一段婚姻走到20年的节点时，这些晚婚的人往往已经50岁了，而在过去，他们这时候可能才40岁出头。”不过，银发离婚率的上升并不意味着老年人的爱情生活就此画上句号。皮尤研究中心2023年的一项调查显示，约14%的60多岁美国人使用过约会软件。另据《纽约时报》报道，在70岁及以上的美国人中，也有12%的人曾使用过这类平台。

paragraphs.contentEn: Divorce rates on the whole have been steadily dropping since 1980, with the Pew Research Center showing 14.4 divorces per 1,000 marriages as of 2023 — compared to the 22.6 divorces per 1,000 marriages nearly 50 years ago. Those reduced rates were largely driven by an increase in the number of people with higher levels of education getting married, and a decrease in those with lower levels, according to Pew. Marriage rates have also declined in recent decades — 69% of adults had been married as of 1970, compared to 50% in 2021.
paragraphs.contentZh: 整体来看，美国的离婚率自1980年以来一直在稳步下降。皮尤研究中心的数据显示，截至2023年，每1000段婚姻中发生14.4起离婚——而在近50年前，这一数字为22.6起。根据皮尤的研究，离婚率下降的主要驱动因素，是高学历人群结婚数量的增加，以及低学历人群结婚数量的相对减少。近几十年来，美国整体的结婚率也在持续走低——在1970年，有69%的成年人处于已婚状态，而到了2021年，这一比例已降至50%。
